subject: Reservation options and bootwave schedule for Lagoon Health
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>

Cc: procurement@lagoonhealth.com
Date: 2029-08-14 09:12 -0700
Subject: Reservation options and bootwave schedule for Lagoon Health

Hi Alyssa / Sam —

Thanks again for the time this week. Per our conversation I put together three reservation options and a recommended onboarding / bootwave schedule that balances cost predictability with runway for your model experiments. Attached: Lagoon_Reserved_Offer_v1.pdf and the onboarding Gantt. High-level options below — these are proposal-level numbers we can tighten after procurement confirms budget range.

1) Flexible Starter (low commitment)
- Min floor: 8 GPUs (NVIDIA A100 equivalent)
- Burst cap: up to 24 GPUs for short bursts
- Ramp: 30-day warm start + on-demand bursts thereafter
- Use-case: light production + aggressive research cycles
- Typical monthly baseline hours: ~25k

2) Flexible Growth (recommended)
- Min floor: 32 GPUs
- Burst cap: up to 64 GPUs
- Ramp: 90-day bootwave (30/60/90 cadence: 25% / 50% / 100% baseline)
- Includes 4 weeks of warm-start credits and priority scheduler during ramp
- Use-case: production + steady experimentation; predictable latency SLO

3) Anchored Slate (heavy commitment)
- Min floor: 64 GPUs
- Burst cap: up to 128 GPUs
- Ramp: 6–12 month staged activation with guaranteed reserved lanes
- Includes onboarding credits, extended SLA, and discounted unit price

Key commercial notes:
- Unit economics shown in the attached pricing_worksheet_lagoon.xlsx; we can convert to committed monthly spend or GPU-hour model.
- Decommit / exit policy: standard 90-day notice; we can include a soft decommit trigger tied to sustained utilization metrics for the Growth option if desired.
- SOC2 and security artifacts are available on request; happy to open an evidence bundle.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Let me know which option you want us to firm up (we can create a 16- or 24-GPU intermediate baseline if budget constraints are tight).
- Procurement: confirm target signature date and any required PO / legal review timeline.

I copied procurement as a heads-up. If helpful I can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough of the offer and the onboarding Gantt.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan

Subject: Re: Reservation options and bootwave schedule for Lagoon Health

Thanks Priya — this is very helpful. A few quick items from our side after a rapid review:

- Budget constraint: current internal guidance puts our preferred baseline closer to 16 GPUs for the first 90 days rather than 32. Can you show a Growth-like option with a 16-GPU min and burst to ~48?
- Ramp cadence: Sam prefers a compressed bootwave (60 days) if unit economics remain reasonable.
- Decommit triggers: procurement needs clarity on whether we can auto-decommit or scale-down without full 90-day penalties if sustained utilization < 30% over a 4-week window. Can Redwood propose a safeguard?
- Compliance: we need SOC 2 Type II evidence and a short runbook describing data retention and KV-cache isolation for private data.

Procurement team — we’ll start an intake and let Pride legal know if needed. Our goal is to conclude commercial terms by Friday EOD (internal ask).

Can you draft a variant with the 16-GPU baseline and explicit decommit conditions? Also include a clear SLA for p95 inference latency at baseline.

Best,
Alyssa
Head of Applied ML, Lagoon Health
alyssa.tan@lagoonhealth.com

Alyssa / Procurement —

Thanks for the feedback. Attached is an updated package that implements the items you requested: Lagoon_Reserved_Offer_v2.pdf and the revised Gantt_onboarding_timeline.xlsx. TL;DR on changes:

- New option: Flexible Growth (16)
  - Min floor: 16 GPUs
  - Burst cap: 48 GPUs
  - Ramp: 90-day bootwave (compressed 60-day option available)
  - Warm-start credits: 2 weeks compute credit applied during onboarding
  - SLA: p95 inference latency at baseline (16-GPU) guaranteed — 350ms for the primary endpoint; detailed SLOs in section 3 of the offer

- Decommit / soft-exit
  - Soft-decommit trigger included: if sustained average utilization < 30% for 4 consecutive weeks, customer may reduce baseline by one tranche (e.g., from 16 -> 8) with a 30-day notice and a pro-rated adjustment fee equal to 10% of the outstanding month commitment.
  - Full decommit (terminate reserved contract) follows the standard 90-day notice; we can offer a reduced 60-day pathway for an early-exit fee that scales with remaining term. Exact numbers in pricing worksheet.

- Commercials: we included a month-to-month benchmark row and 12/24 month committed pricing. The effective blended rate for the 16-min baseline is included in pricing_worksheet_lagoon.xlsx; the net effective after credits is highlighted.

Action items for Lagoon:
- Please review the attached Offer_v2 and confirm whether you prefer the 60-day compressed ramp or canonical 90-day bootwave.
- If terms look good, sign via DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sign?doc=lagoon_offer_v2. I also linked the HubSpot deal: https://redwood.hubspot.com/deal/LAGOON-278.

If procurement wants a short call to review the decommit mechanics and SLA language I can join with Marcus and Ben.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this one.
